Counsel for Opposite Party :- A.G.A.
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J. 
1. Heard Sri Vinod Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for Revisionist and learned A.G.A. for State.
2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by the judgments and orders dated 21.04.1990 and 23.09.1985.

The Judicial Magistrate, Economic Offence, Agra vide judgment and order dated 23.09.1985 convicted the Revisionist under Section 7/16 of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as ?Act, 1954) and sentenced him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment with fine Rs.1000/- and in case of default in payment of fine, he was further to undergo three months rigorous imprisonment.

Being aggrieved he preferred an appeal before the Court of IV Additional Sessions Judge, Agra (hereinafter referred to as ?Appellate Court?) in Criminal Appeal No.173 of 1985 and Appellate Court vide judgment and order dated 21.04.1990 while dismissing the appeal has confirmed the judgment and order of conviction against Revisionist passed by the Trial Court.

sentences.text: It is contended by learned counsel for Revisionist that when Food Inspector was taking sample, it was mentioned by Revisionist that he is selling mixed milk of cow and buffalo but that has been ignored and the sample has been taken as that of buffalo's milk and same has been chemically examined accordingly.
Therefore, entire prosecution case falls for the reason that sample was taken of mixed milk of buffalo and cow, hence the ratio of buffalo's milk could not have been assessed.
Learned counsel for Revisionist further submitted that in this regard a defence witness was also examined.

4. From record it is evident that Courts below have considered this aspect and found that evidence of DW 1 Kumar Sen, who had stated that Revisionist disclosed to the Food Inspector at the time of taking of sample that it was mixed milk of cow and buffalo, is not reliable as the entire inspection documents are in respect of buffalo's milk and said defence was taken for the first time in the Court.
5. DW 1 was produced and stated that he was present at the site at the time of inspection and accused-Revisionist stated that it was mixed milk of cow and buffalo.
It appears that Trial Court did not find presence of DW 1 at the site, doubtful.

If that be so, in order to disbelieve the statement of DW-1, I find that no reason has been given in the judgment of Trial Court and on this aspect Appellate Court has not given any finding and this aspect has been completely overlooked by Appellate Court.
Trial Court has referred to document of inspection ignoring statement of DW-1, but had given no reason as to why statement of DW-1 is not reliable.

6. In view thereof, it cannot be said that the prosecution has been successful to prove adulteration in the matter, since, deficiency has been found in the context of milk of buffalo while at the time of taking sample it was mentioned by accused-Revisionist that it was mixed milk of cow and buffalo.
7. Revision is accordingly allowed.
Judgments and orders dated 21.04.1990 and 23.09.1985 passed by Courts below are hereby set aside.
8. Certify this Judgement to Lower Court immediately.
